hypothesis: If Darwin is right, no amphibian species (frog, toad, newt or caecilian) is native to any truly oceanic island, i.e. one that has never been connected to a continent. Amphibians introduced by people do persist on many of those islands.
pass_criterion: Using the oceanic-island list fixed below, 0 of the 16 island groups have an amphibian taxon with a native or endemic status. That status must come from GBIF establishmentMeans=NATIVE or from the range statement for a species in the AmphibiaWeb or IUCN cross-check. Records are checked after removing coordinate and country errors and records from museum or captive-held specimens (basisOfRecord FOSSIL_SPECIMEN, MATERIAL_SAMPLE, or from zoos). In addition, at least 8 of the 16 groups must have amphibian occurrences flagged INTRODUCED or INVASIVE, or with an introduced status in the species accounts. This shows that conditions there are suitable. The claim is supported only if both conditions hold.
fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if 2 or more of the 16 pre-listed oceanic island groups have a native amphibian species. Each such species must be confirmed by two independent sources (GBIF native-flagged records plus an AmphibiaWeb or IUCN range statement) and have at least 3 verified records. It is also refuted if fewer than 8 of the 16 groups have any introduced amphibian, because then the 'introduced frogs thrive' part is not supported. A single native group gives an inconclusive result, to be reported as a named exception to the generalization.
interpretation: 'Batrachians' means the modern class Amphibia: Anura (frogs and toads) and Caudata (newts and salamanders), and also Gymnophiona (caecilians) as a conservative extension. 'Oceanic islands' means islands of volcanic or coralline origin that have never been joined to a continent. The pre-registered list of 16 groups is: Hawaii, Galápagos, Azores, Madeira, Canary Islands, Cape Verde, Bermuda, St Helena, Ascension, Tristan da Cunha, Society Islands, Marquesas, Kerguelen, Mascarenes (Mauritius, Réunion, Rodrigues), Easter Island and Pitcairn. Continental-fragment islands are excluded because they are not oceanic in Darwin's sense: New Zealand, Seychelles, Madagascar, Japan, the Greater Antilles and New Caledonia. The Fiji, Samoa and Solomon islands arcs are also excluded, because their oceanic status is disputed and their native Cornufer/Platymantis frogs would otherwise be decided by definition. The modern reinterpretation is that the claim becomes a testable range statement. Native status is read from GBIF establishmentMeans and the country/island fields (countryCode, island, islandGroup). Introduced status is read from the same field. The mechanism, that sea-water kills amphibians and their spawn, is not tested here. Only the pattern of absence and the suitability of the islands are tested.

dataset.name: GBIF Occurrence Data: Amphibia (class Amphibia, taxon key 131)
dataset.publisher: GBIF, the Global Biodiversity Information Facility
dataset.why_it_fits: GBIF serves Amphibia occurrence records through a free API and downloads. The fields used are: scientificName, taxonKey, class, countryCode, island, islandGroup, decimalLatitude, decimalLongitude, establishmentMeans, basisOfRecord and year. The records can be filtered by country, island and island group, so they can be tallied for each pre-listed oceanic island group. The establishmentMeans values separate native from introduced records. GBIF as a whole has no single DOI, so doi is null. A download would receive its own DOI at the time it is made. AmphibiaWeb (https://amphibiaweb.org) is used only to cross-check the status of any flagged species.
